articles.title: Nanocoder plugins: JavaScript that can veto a tool call from inside the agent
articles.focus: A hands-on tour of the new .nanocoder/plugins/*.mjs extension point - the five hooks (tool.execute.before, tool.execute.after, session.compacting, tui.prompt.append, permission.asked), how a JS plugin differs from a shell hook (it can block a tool, annotate a result, deny a permission prompt outright, and append prompt context), and the safety contract that keeps it from becoming a footgun (loads only in a trusted directory, a throwing or 30-second-stuck plugin is logged and ignored rather than blocking the agent, and it cannot approve a tool or add new ones).

articles.title: How Nanocoder reads a 3000-line test log and hands the model only the failures
articles.focus: A behind-the-scenes look at the failure capsule: why a head-and-tail cut of a failing Jest/Vitest/Mocha/AVA or tsc run used to drop the assertion detail printed in the middle of the log, how the capsule keeps each failing test's title, location and expected/received diff, how the original command is safely narrowed to a single test and re-run once to tell a real failure from a flaky or order-dependent one, and the deliberate limits that stop the re-run from repeating pre/post package hooks or running arbitrary shell constructs.

articles.title: Measuring an agent: the eval harness that scores a released tag, not your tree
articles.focus: An explainer of the new benchmarks/agent harness - it shells out to nanocoder --plain --json run so a published tag and the working tree can be compared with the same fixture set, it scores pass/fail, steps, tokens and cost per task, and its six vendored fixtures carry machine-checkable assertions plus distractor files so an agent working from degraded context fails the assertion instead of quietly finishing cheaper, with every result stamped with the fixture-set id and a content hash of the fixtures.
